articles.title: From $3 million to $38 million: Brittany Mahomes’ soccer team sees revenue skyrocket
articles.summary: Brittany Mahomes has another reason to celebrate as the Kansas City Current continues to make noise both on and off the soccer field.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes has another reason to celebrate as the Kansas City Current continues to make noise both on and off the soccer field. The KC Current had a huge day on October 25, when a record 18,000 fans gathered across CPKC Stadium and Current Landing for the team's final home game of the season. And while the crowd came out to support the team, there is a much bigger business story behind the celebration.The team, co-owned by Brittany and her husband, Patrick Mahomes, is now valued at a whopping $325 million, according to Forbes' 2026 NWSL valuations. That is an 18% jump from its $275 million valuation in 2025. Not bad for a soccer club that began playing in 2021!Brittany Mahomes: From a new Soccer team to a $325 million businessBrittany is not just attached to the KC Current because of her famous NFL husband. The former soccer player helped bring the club to Kansas City when it was founded in 2020 alongside owners Angie and Chris Long.Her own soccer background makes the project especially meaningful. Brittany played soccer in college and later played professionally in Iceland before turning her attention to other ventures. Patrick joined the ownership group in 2022, making the club a family affair. But Brittany's involvement started before that, and the team's growth has given her plenty to celebrate.The KC Current's growth has been impressive. The team generated an estimated $38 million in revenue in 2025, according to Forbes, tying with Angel City FC for the highest revenue in the NWSL. The club's purpose-built home has played a major role in that success. CPKC Stadium opened in 2024 after an investment of around $140 million, giving the team new ways to make money through tickets, premium seating, concessions, sponsorships and other events.For comparison, Forbes reported that the Current generated only around $3 million in revenue during its first season in 2021. That makes the jump to $38 million in estimated annual revenue a remarkable change in just a few years. Of course, the team's $325 million valuation is not the same as the money Brittany personally owns or earns. It represents an estimate of the club's overall value.The 18,000 fan celebration was about more than SoccerThe October 25 home finale against the Washington Spirit gave the Current another reason to celebrate. The team won 2-1, while the combined crowd at the stadium and the outdoor Current Landing viewing area reached a record 18,000.Around 6,000 fans watched from outside the stadium, showing how the club has found ways to bring even more people into its matchday experience. The Current had also secured a playoff spot before the game, adding another reason for fans to turn up and celebrate.The crowd does not mean the team made a specific amount of money that day, and there are no confirmed figures for the match's total earnings. But a packed stadium and a growing fan base can help a club attract sponsors, sell tickets and build its business over time.For Brittany, the latest milestone is another reminder that the soccer venture she helped launch has grown into one of the biggest businesses in women's professional soccer. And with the Current continuing to expand its reach, the Mahomes family's sports portfolio has plenty more room to grow.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “Not caring about low character players”: Chiefs face backlash over Justin Tucker signing
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are facing backlash after signing Justin Tucker to their practice squad.
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs are facing backlash after signing Justin Tucker to their practice squad. While the move gives the team another option at kicker, it has also sparked a heated debate among fans, with some questioning the decision and others coming to Tucker’s defense.Why is Justin Tucker’s signing causing outrage amongst fans?For those living under a rock, Tucker, widely regarded as one of the NFL’s most successful kickers who has faced sexual misconduct allegations involving massage therapists. He denied the allegations, and the NFL later suspended him for 10 games for violating its personal conduct policy following its investigation.He was not criminally charged in connection with the allegations. However, the absence of criminal charges does not mean a court determined that the allegations were false. The NFL’s disciplinary process was separate from the criminal justice system.This background has made his move to Kansas City particularly controversial, with some fans questioning whether the Chiefs should have signed him while others believe he deserves an opportunity to return to the league.The reaction was a whole spectrum, with fans criticizing the Chiefs’ front office, discussing the allegations against Tucker and questioning how the team’s decision should be viewed.One user shared a short but sarcastic reaction, writing, “Chiefs front office.” Although the comment was brief, it was to criticize the team’s management for bringing Tucker into the organization.Another one commented, “Andy Reid has a long history of not caring about low character players, low morals coach, no one ever talks about it.”For fans, the move is not just about football but also about the message the team sends by giving Tucker another opportunity in the NFL. However, not everyone agreed with the criticism.While some supporters questioned the Chiefs’ decision, others argued that Tucker should not be judged without considering the legal outcome of the allegations against him.One user pushed back against the criticism, writing, “Ok… anyone can acuse anyone of anything. What were the legal repercussions and what did the legal system determine?”The Chiefs added Tucker to their practice squad as the team dealt with concerns about its kicking situation. Harrison Butker remains the team's established kicker, meaning Tucker's arrival does not automatically make him the starter. The signing gives Kansas City another option if its kicking problems continue. However, the team must now deal with the public reaction surrounding its decision.For now, the backlash shows that Tucker's arrival is about more than his performance on the field. With fans split between criticizing the Chiefs and defending the kicker, the decision has created another talking point for the franchise.Whether Tucker eventually earns a spot on the active roster remains to be seen, but his signing has already sparked a debate that extends well beyond football.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chiefs billionaire heiress Gracie Hunt pushes fashion boundaries as her signature look continues to evolve
articles.summary: Gracie Hunt has built a public image that goes well beyond her family's connection to the Kansas City Chiefs.
articles.body: Gracie Hunt has built a public image that goes well beyond her family's connection to the Kansas City Chiefs. As the daughter of team owner Clark Hunt, she grew up around football, but her personal style has taken its own path. From casual sportswear and running shorts to sparkling gowns, bold red outfits and metallic dresses, her wardrobe has changed with each new chapter of her life. Her journey also reflects her experience in beauty pageants, her early love of soccer and her growing presence in the fashion world.Gracie Hunt’s early style and beauty pageant transformationBefore becoming known for glamorous outfits, Gracie Hunt preferred comfortable clothes. Older photos on her Instagram show her wearing trainers, shorts, simple tops and minimal makeup. At the time, her interests leaned more towards sports than fashion.Soccer was her first love. In an interview with People in 2025, Gracie explained, "I wanted to be the next Mia Hamm, and soccer was my first love. ... My grandfather, Lamar Hunt, actually helped bring Major League Soccer to the United States."However, four concussions forced her to reconsider her sporting ambitions. She later turned to beauty pageants, following in the footsteps of her mother, Tavia Hunt, who won Miss Kansas USA in 1993.The transition was not instant. Tavia initially questioned whether pageantry suited her daughter's sporty manner. As Gracie recalled in an interview with the New York Post, her mother told her, "I'm not sure [pageants are a good idea] because you walk like a soccer tomboy, but we can give it a shot."With her mother's guidance, Gracie refined her walk and began experimenting with more formal clothing. In 2016, she won Miss Teen Texas International, wearing elegant gowns that marked a clear shift from her earlier wardrobe. She won the title again in 2018, further establishing her presence in the pageant world.Pink, purple and scarlet soon became defining colours. Her outfits featured sparkling details, statement earrings and carefully styled hair, creating the polished look associated with beauty queens.From metallic dresses to Kansas City Chiefs-inspired fashionAs Gracie Hunt's public profile grew, her fashion choices expanded beyond pageant gowns. During the winter of 2019, she embraced coordinated outfits, including black coats, fur-lined boots and matching separates. She also experimented with crop tops and bold looks during a trip to Paris.The pandemic brought another change. Gracie returned to athletic clothing, wearing running shorts, sweatshirts and yoga pants while preparing for the Miss USA competition. She also worked with a walking coach to improve her stage presence.In 2021, after winning Miss Kansas USA, she combined polished outfits with her charitable commitments. Her wardrobe included a royal blue blazer and matching shorts, paired with heels and her crown.Metallic fashion later became a favourite. In 2023, Gracie wore sparkling gold and silver outfits to high-profile events, including the NFL Commissioner's Super Bowl party. A silver puffer jacket at the Chiefs' Super Bowl parade also blended her fashion interests with team pride.By the 2024 to 2025 season, red and gold had become prominent in her game-day wardrobe. She launched a clothing line with Wear by Erin Andrews, including a red Chiefs corset with gold chain straps.Gracie Hunt's style evolution reflects more than changing trends. Each phase connects to her interests, experiences and public roles. Whether she wears athletic basics, a dramatic gown or Chiefs-inspired fashion, she continues to shape an image that combines family legacy, pageantry and personal expression.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce's $5.35 million Ohio mansion plans hit another costly snag over an unexpected property issue
articles.summary: Travis Kelce wanted to put down roots in the Cleveland area, close to the place he has called home for much of his life.
articles.body: Travis Kelce wanted to put down roots in the Cleveland area, close to the place he has called home for much of his life. But the Kansas City Chiefs tight end and his plans for a private family life have reportedly run into an unexpected obstacle. His $5.35 million Ohio mansion has become the centre of a neighbourhood dispute over proposed security upgrades. The controversy has reportedly left Kelce and Taylor Swift upset, with concerns about privacy, safety and relations with their new neighbours adding pressure to their plans for the property.Travis Kelce's Ohio mansion security plans spark neighbourhood disputeThe dispute centres on proposed changes to the couple's property in Bratenahl, Cleveland. According to reports, the plans include a six-foot fence and additional trees intended to create a stronger barrier around the mansion.For Kelce, the move to Ohio carries personal significance. The NFL star grew up in the area and reportedly wanted to build a family life close to his roots. However, the proposed changes have drawn objections from some residents, who have raised concerns about the impact on the neighbourhood.The disagreement reportedly extends beyond the fence itself. A shared sewer line has also become part of the discussions, with the couple offering to cover costs associated with relocating the old pipe to accommodate the planned landscaping and security work.Despite those efforts, the situation has attracted unwanted attention. Reports have also described drones circling the property before the security plans were finalised, adding another layer to the couple's reported concerns about privacy.A source quoted by Heat World said the couple had tried to avoid conflict and were willing to pay for work that might otherwise have been shared with neighbours.“Taylor and Travis are genuinely very upset about this. The last thing they wanted was to have any sort of friction with their neighbours. They have tried so hard to make sure people would be happy - already paid for all sorts of work that might normally be split between the neighbours and, knowing Taylor, she’ll gladly pay for anything else that the neighbours might need as a result of the trees they are adding to their property.”Travis Kelce's privacy concerns go beyond neighbourhood objectionsThe disagreement also raises a broader question about how public figures can protect their homes while respecting the concerns of the people living nearby.For Kelce, whose NFL career and relationship with Swift attract considerable attention, maintaining a secure private space may be an important part of establishing a home away from the spotlight. The reported security proposals are intended to address more than curious onlookers, according to the source.“It's incredibly stressful; this isn’t just about wanting privacy from all the fans and lookie-loos - there are stalkers and genuine threats to their safety that they need to prepare for. It’s a little shocking to them that there’s no understanding of that - these changes aren’t cosmetic, they’re the difference between Taylor feeling safe in her home and being at risk.”The comments reflect the couple's reported concerns, although the specific threats have not been independently detailed in the available account.For now, the Ohio mansion dispute highlights the challenge of balancing residential security with neighbourhood expectations. Whether the proposed changes move forward remains unclear, leaving questions about the couple's plans for their Cleveland-area home unanswered.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: NFL Power Rankings: Who Is the New No. 1 Team After Chiefs, 49ers’ Losses?
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings have taken over the top spot in the NFL power rankings after Week 7 delivered losses for the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings have taken over the top spot in the NFL power rankings after Week 7 delivered losses for the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers. Minnesota's 16-10 win over Indianapolis left it as the league's only undefeated team, giving the club a rise as the season moves forward.

The Vikings improved to 6-0 with a performance built around their defense, which continues to set the team's identity. Minnesota climbed three places, moving from fourth to first, while other lists also placed the club near the top. The shift reflects both the team's unbeaten record and the stumbles of previously favored contenders.

Defensive coordinator Brian Flores has helped create an aggressive unit that has made life difficult for opposing offenses. Minnesota held Indianapolis to 10 points and limited the Colts to six through three quarters, keeping the game within reach even as its own offense struggled to find consistent rhythm. The defense's ability to produce pressure and disrupt plays has become a central reason for the Vikings' early success.

The offense, however, remains a significant question. Minnesota has not consistently matched its defensive production, and the passing game has struggled to generate yardage at a high level. Quarterback Kyler Murray will need to deliver more steady results, particularly as the schedule grows more demanding and opponents have additional time to prepare for the Vikings' defensive strengths.

Minnesota Vikings Become New No. 1 Team in the Latest NFL Power Rankings

Minnesota has emerged as the top team in the league at this point of the season. This is detailed more in the latest power rankings posted by the league's official website.

Week 7 claimed two of the three remaining undefeated teams in the NFL, leaving the Vikings as the last unbeaten squad standing. They climbed to the mountaintop by winning in their familiar fashion, with defense leading the way. Brian Flores' unit is unquestionably elite and getting more creative with its approach each week. If the offense ever catches up, Minnesota will become a strong Super Bowl favorite.

That challenge could determine how long Minnesota stays atop the rankings. The team's upcoming slate includes several difficult matchups, offering a test of whether its undefeated start can translate into sustained dominance. The Vikings have earned their place through six wins, but the margin for error may narrow as they face stronger competition and need more balance on offense.

Minnesota is the league's standard-bearer, powered by a defense that has repeatedly kept games under control. The top ranking is a milestone, but maintaining it will require the offense to improve and the defense to continue its high level of play. The Vikings have seized the opportunity created by Week 7, and the next stretch will show whether they can hold on firmly.

articles.title: Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy says wife Mia is 'doing great' 3 months after surviving shooting
articles.summary: Bieniemy said Thursday that rehab is going well for Mia, who was shot in the chest and arm in July. Their son, Elijah, was arrested in connection with the ca...
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy has shared a positive update on his wife Mia, three months after she was shot in their family home .

When speaking to reporters on Thursday, Bieniemy said that Mia was doing well enough to go on a trip with friends this past weekend.

"She's doing great. She actually went on a trip this weekend," Bieniemy said. "She was a rockstar, obviously. "Her rehab has been going great. She actually had an opportunity to come out here and hang out and I'm sure I got on her nerves," he joked.

"She's doing great. She actually went on a trip this weekend," Bieniemy said. "She was a rockstar, obviously.

"Her rehab has been going great. She actually had an opportunity to come out here and hang out and I'm sure I got on her nerves," he joked.

Mia, 57, was shot in the arm and chest at their family home in Loudoun County, Virginia, on July 26. She was hospitalized with multiple gunshot wounds.

Elijah Bieniemy, the 27-year-old son of Eric and Mia, was arrested and charged with the shooting the following day.

In August, three weeks after the shooting, Bieniemy returned to practice and told reporters that Mia was on the "road to recovery."

"It's one of the main reasons why I'm back here, because of her recovery," Eric Bieniemy said. "She's truly a soldier. She's a saint and it's been incredible to watch. But I know I was driving her and a bunch of my family members crazy in the house, so she was like, 'You have my blessing to leave.' It was time to get back."

Last month, Elijah Bieniemy was found fit to stand trial after a psychological evaluation. A public defender who represented Elijah earlier in the trial (he now has new representation) wrote in a filing that "the defendant appears to suffer from significant mental health issues."

Eric Bieniemy, a decorated offensive coach, returned to the Chiefs' sideline this season as offensive coordinator, a role he served in from 2018-2022.

He served in various assistant coaching roles for the Washington Commanders, UCLA and Chicago Bears in between stints in Kansas City.

articles.title: Packers’ Josh Jacobs Had an ‘Interesting’ Comment Ahead of His First Lambeau Field Game in 2026 Season
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs has finally seen action in the 2026 NFL season after getting removed from the NFL’s commissioner exempt list. Jaco...
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs has finally seen action in the 2026 NFL season after getting removed from the NFL's commissioner exempt list.

Jacobs missed the first six weeks of the season while he was placed on that list, stemming from his arrest in the offseason over misdemeanor charges after an altercation with his then-girlfriend in May.

The three-time Pro Bowl tailback returned to action in Green Bay's Week 7 game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field in Detroit, and he's about to make his first appearance at Lambeau Field in Green Bay for a Week 8 Thursday Night Football showdown against the visiting Carolina Panthers .

"It's going to be interesting. Obviously, like primetime, Lambeau Field, Thursday night, it's gonna be electric," the former Alabama Crimson Tide star running back told reporters via ESPN's Rob Demovsky. "Looking forward to seeing our fans. Going out there and playing some good ball."

Will Jacobs, Packers' Rushing Attack Shine in Week 8?

It will be interesting to see what kind of reception Jacobs will get from Packers fans. He was booed by Detroit fans in Week 7, and he could hear the same thing from at least a few fans in Green Bay.

In any case, Jacobs is expected to help Green Bay's run game that has been arguably the worst in the NFL thus far.

The Packers are averaging fewer than 60 rushing yards per game and are also last in the NFL with only 2.9 yards per carry.

Against the Lions, Jacobs and company came up with only 60 rushing yards on 19 carries. Jacobs had 36 rushing yards on 11 carries in that contest.

However, there is a reason to believe that Green Bay will have a great night on the ground versus the Panthers, as Carolina is allowing over 150 rushing yards per game.

articles.title: Mina Kimes’ Captionless Post After Chiefs’ Justin Tucker Signing Sparks Reactions
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs’ decision to sign veteran NFL kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad has caught a lot of people by surprise, especially because...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs' decision to sign veteran NFL kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad has caught a lot of people by surprise, especially because of his history — off the field.

Tucker was cut by the Baltimore Ravens in May of 2025 amid sexual misconduct accusations from over a dozen massage therapists. He was later suspended for 10 games by the NFL before being eligible for reinstatement last November.

Tucker was able to get tryouts with the New Orleans Saints and the Indianapolis Colts since, but wasn't signed.

On Thursday, it was reported that the Chiefs were signing Tucker to a practice squad contract, a move that raised eyebrows.

Following the news of Tucker's addition to the Chiefs' practice squad, ESPN's Mina Kimes posted on X without a caption, attaching a screenshot of a report detailing the accusations against the kicker.

Kimes didn't need a caption to sum up what she really feels about this development involving the Chiefs and Tucker.

It also clearly turned heads online, with nearly 40,000 likes and over a thousand comments made on her post at the time of this writing.

Chiefs Add Tucker as Insurance Behind Struggling First Option

Kansas City felt it had to add another kicker as insurance amid the struggles of Harrison Butker.

So far in the 2026 NFL season, Butker has gone 11/16 on his field-goal tries, and two of his misses came in Week 7's 20-3 Kansas City loss to the reigning Super Bowl champions Seattle Seahawks on the road.

What's interesting, however, is that Tucker wasn't great either in the most recent season he played in the NFL. In 2024, he went 22/30 on his kicks for a 73.3 percent success rate — the lowest of his career.

Kansas City enters Week 8 of the 2026 season with a 5-1 record and will face the Denver Broncos in a road game this coming Sunday.

articles.title: Chicago Just Changed the Entire Super Bowl Race! Jeffery Simmons Could Make the Bears Nearly Impossible to Beat!
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears just sent a massive warning to the rest of the NFL, and it might have completely changed the Super Bowl picture. Chicago pulled off one of...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears just sent a massive warning to the rest of the NFL, and it might have completely changed the Super Bowl picture.

Chicago pulled off one of the biggest moves of the season by acquiring Tennessee Titans superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons in a blockbuster trade. The Bears gave up their 2027 and 2028 first-round picks, along with a 2027 fourth-round selection, to bring the four-time Pro Bowler to Chicago. They also received a 2028 fifth-round pick in the deal.

And honestly, this is the kind of move that can turn a good football team into a legitimate championship contender.

The Bears entered the season with plenty of offensive firepower behind Caleb Williams and head coach Ben Johnson. At 5-2, they had already shown they could compete with some of the best teams in the league. However, their biggest weakness remained on the defensive side of the football, particularly when it came to creating pressure up the middle.

That problem just got a whole lot smaller.

Simmons has already recorded four sacks, 38 tackles and six tackles for loss through seven games this season. He is coming off a dominant 2025 campaign in which he recorded 11 sacks and earned First-Team All-Pro honors.

Now imagine putting that kind of player alongside Montez Sweat and Grady Jarrett.

Opposing quarterbacks are going to have a nightmare trying to find time in the pocket. Simmons gives Chicago an elite interior presence who can disrupt plays, collapse the pocket and make life easier for everyone else on the defensive line.

The move has already sent shockwaves through the betting market. Chicago's Super Bowl odds improved from +1400 to +1100 at BetMGM, putting the Bears among the top teams in the championship race. Some sportsbooks have moved them even higher.

But the biggest takeaway is that Chicago isn't just hoping to compete anymore. General manager Ryan Poles is making it clear that this team believes its championship window is wide open.

Giving up two first-round picks is an enormous gamble, and the Bears are going to need Simmons to make a major impact for that price to pay off. Still, when you have a young quarterback, an explosive offense and a defense that just added one of the best players at his position, sitting back and waiting isn't always the answer.

The Bears have officially pushed their chips into the middle of the table.

San Francisco, Seattle, Los Angeles and the rest of the NFC contenders better take notice. Chicago just made one of the boldest moves of the entire season, and there is a real argument that the Bears now have everything needed to make a run at the Lombardi Trophy.

articles.title: Tom Brady's charity work spans $46.5 million, African poverty relief and sick children's wishes
articles.summary: Tom Brady built his name on record-breaking performances and six Super Bowl victories with the New England Patriots.
articles.body: Tom Brady built his name on record-breaking performances and six Super Bowl victories with the New England Patriots. Yet his influence has reached far beyond the football field. The NFL legend has used his fame, time and resources to support people facing challenges that often go unnoticed. From helping athletes access healthcare to supporting children with serious illnesses, Brady has backed causes that aim to create lasting change. His charitable work also reaches communities in Africa, where an eye-opening visit helped shape his understanding of global poverty and the need for greater support.Tom Brady's charity work supports people with disabilities and global communitiesOne of Brady's most significant charitable commitments has been to Best Buddies International, a nonprofit that helps people with intellectual and developmental disabilities build friendships, find jobs and become more involved in their communities.According to Borgen Magazine, Brady helped raise $46.5 million for the organisation over two decades. He also served as an honorary co-chair of its annual cycling, running and walking event for 16 years before becoming a global ambassador in December 2019. His involvement went beyond fundraising, with appearances at events helping bring attention to the organisation's mission.Brady also turned his attention to poverty in Africa. In 2004, he travelled to Ghana and Uganda with Debt, AIDS, Trade, Africa (DATA), an organisation that worked to raise awareness of poverty and development issues across the continent.During the trip, he visited schools, medical clinics and an HIV/AIDS clinic in Uganda that received support from US foreign aid. Seeing the challenges faced by local communities gave him a closer look at how international assistance could make a difference.Reflecting on the experience, Brady said, “I saw the best and brightest of the human spirit in the face of incredible poverty that most of us just can’t comprehend. When you see what CAN be done, it’s impossible to not be driven to do more — the needs are still overwhelming.”His words highlighted the gap between the resources available in wealthier countries and the urgent needs facing vulnerable communities.Tom Brady's TB12 Foundation and Make-A-Wish support athletes and childrenBrady also established a charitable initiative of his own. In 2015, he founded the TB12 Foundation to help athletes pursue their performance goals by improving access to health and wellness resources.The foundation focused on people from low-income backgrounds and athletes who might otherwise struggle to afford the support they needed. Its fundraising efforts included an annual marathon in Boston, which raised more than $125,000 in the year cited by Borgen Magazine to help provide healthcare resources.Brady has also supported the Make-A-Wish Foundation, which creates memorable experiences for children living with serious illnesses. In 2019, he and his New England Patriots teammates welcomed five children, showed them around the team's stadium and treated them to dinner.These efforts reveal another side of Brady's public life. His charitable work has combined financial contributions with personal involvement, helping organisations reach people who need support. While his football achievements remain central to his legacy, his work beyond the game shows how an athlete's platform can also draw attention to disability inclusion, healthcare access and global poverty.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. The NFL is back and so are the Yahoo Fantasy x Arena Club Slab Packs!

Loaded with top performers and fantasy stars, the Yahoo Fantasy x Arena Club Slab packs will be available each week during the regular season for collectors and fans to digitally rip.

For those new to Arena Club , it is a new way of collecting. As the premier tech-powered marketplace and grading platform, Arena Club brings the physical experience of card collecting into the digital age. Users can purchase and open virtual packs of real, pre-graded cards ("slabs"), buy and sell on the marketplace and manage their card showrooms all in one place. Each Arena Club Slab Pack displays the full lineup of potential cards and the likelihood of ripping each.

Yahoo Fantasy Slab Packs contain graded NFL trading cards curated by Arena Club. Fans can purchase a slab pack, each containing a graded card of an NFL player, via the Arena Club platform. The packs will feature "Chase Cards" of the top fantasy football performers of the week across the QB, RB, WR and TE positions. These "Chase Cards" are the rarest, most valuable cards in the Yahoo Fantasy Slab Packs, worth up to 3-4x the price of the pack.

You can head to ArenaClub.com or the Arena Club app and use the promo code YAHOO20 at checkout for 20% off your first slab pack or card purchase.

Joe Burrow, Bengals – No QB in the league has been hotter than Joe Cool the past two weeks. The Bengals star is making a midseason MVP push with eight touchdowns and zero interceptions in back-to-back wins for Cincinnati.

Bo Nix, Broncos – It hasn't been the biggest statistical season for Nix, but he has the Broncos sitting at 5-2 and coming off a game where he made big plays with his arm and legs, with a season-long 52-yard pass and 62-yard run in a 30-16 win over Arizona.

articles.title: Christian Watson Returns from Hospital After Scary Injury During Packers vs. Panthers
articles.summary: Christian Watson suffered a serious injury after exiting Thursday night's game against the Carolina Panthers, but it could not keep him away for too long.
articles.body:
Christian Watson suffered a serious injury after exiting Thursday night's game against the Carolina Panthers, but it could not keep him away for too long.

After landing awkwardly after making a catch, the Green Bay Packers wide receiver walked off the field and into the locker room on his own power, but was taken to a local hospital for "precautionary testing," the team announced .

He was later cleared to leave the hospital and return to the sideline in dramatic fashion by the third quarter.

He was back on the field before the start of the fourth.

The initial injury came at the end of a long completion in the second quarter:

The team officially referred to it as a chest injury when Watson exited the game. He told Kaylee Hartun of Amazon Prime after the game that he didn't want to go to the hospital, but he was told that he needed to go after spitting up blood.

Watson was putting together a fantastic game before the injury, recording six receptions for 100 yards. His last play before exiting was a 53-yard reception off a pass from Jordan Love.

While the severity of the injury is not yet known, any time missed by Watson would be detrimental to the Packers' offense. The fifth-year receiver is well on his way to a career season, coming into Thursday's game with the seventh-most receiving yards (595), the second-most receiving touchdowns (6) and the third-best yards-per-reception average (17.5) in the league this year.

With the addition of his 100 receiving yards against the Panthers, Watson has now eclipsed his career-high in just seven games.

The Packers have had a middle-of-the-pack offense so far this year, averaging 328.4 yards and 20.6 points per game so far, and losing Watson would make things ever worse.

Watson, a second-round pick in 2022, has unfortunately dealt with injuries throughout his young career. He missed a handful of games as a rookie before playing just nine games in 2023 with various injuries. He played 15 games in 2024 but suffered a torn ACL at the end of the season, forcing him to miss the first seven games of the 2025 campaign.

Watson will look to avoid another serious injury this year as he looks to continue his breakout season.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ latest move with Brittany reveals another side of his Kansas City life

articles.body: Patrick Mahomes’ influence in Kansas City reaches well beyond the football field. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, have launched a new initiative aimed at helping families manage food allergies when dining out. Their project, called 15 and Fare, brings Mahomes’ charitable foundation together with Food Allergy Research & Education (FARE) to encourage safer food preparation at local restaurants. The effort also has a personal connection for the couple, whose two eldest children have food allergies. It offers a closer look at how their family experiences are shaping their work in the community.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany launch 15 and FARE to improve restaurant food safetyThe initiative has reached an important milestone with Joe’s Kansas City Bar-B-Que becoming its first recognized restaurant partner. The restaurant announced the achievement on October 27, highlighting its efforts to train staff in food allergy preparation and handling.The recognition is based on practical steps rather than a simple endorsement. Participating restaurants must train at least 90% of their food service staff, complete monthly on-site audits for three consecutive months, establish a written food allergy management policy and provide clear allergen information on their menus.These requirements address a concern that many diners face every time they eat outside their homes. For families managing food allergies, ordering a meal can involve detailed questions about ingredients, preparation methods and the risk of cross-contact. A restaurant's willingness to answer those questions matters, but consistent procedures can make the experience safer and less stressful.Joe’s Kansas City Bar-B-Que acknowledged the significance of its recognition in an announcement shared online."We are really proud today to post this sign up. Joe's is the first restaurant to be recognized as 15 & Fare approved. Over the past two years our managment staff in our restaurants have become certified in food allergy prep & handling."This initiative was started by @patrickmahomes & @brittanylynne and their charity @15andMahomies. Now we want others to join us! We'll be sharing soon how other restaurants can join 15 & Fare!"The restaurant's recognition gives the program a tangible starting point. The next challenge is to persuade more local businesses to adopt the same standards and make allergy awareness part of their daily operations.Their children's food allergies give the initiative a personal purposeFor Patrick and Brittany, the project is rooted in their own family experiences. Their two eldest children, Sterling and Bronze, have food allergies, giving the couple a personal understanding of the concerns parents face when they cannot be certain how a meal has been prepared.That connection helps explain why the initiative goes beyond restaurant recognition. Through a partnership between the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation and Food Allergy Research & Education, known as FARE, the program also aims to expand access to education, support and resources across Kansas City. Training opportunities extend to community food banks and pantries, where food safety can be just as important.The work also adds another dimension to Mahomes' public role. His achievements with the Chiefs have made him one of the NFL's most recognizable players, but this effort focuses on a problem that families deal with far from the stadium. Brittany's involvement reflects that same personal commitment, turning an experience within their household into a community effort.The couple cannot remove the risks associated with food allergies, and a restaurant's approval should not replace a diner's own precautions. Still, better training, clearer menus and stronger preparation practices can help families make informed choices.For Kansas City, the real measure of success will be whether more restaurants follow Joe's example. One recognized business is an encouraging start. articles.title: “You can judge a person's character pretty early”: How Travis Kelce quietly gifted Chiefs coach Porter Ellett two Nike self-lacing shoes following his heartbreaking childhood accident
articles.summary: Travis Kelce did not make a big announcement when he helped Kansas City Chiefs coach Porter Ellett.
articles.body: Travis Kelce did not make a big announcement when he helped Kansas City Chiefs coach Porter Ellett. He simply remembered a conversation about shoes and turned it into a thoughtful surprise. In 2017, Kelce arranged two pairs of Nike's self-lacing sneakers for Ellett, who had lost the use of his right arm as a child. Years later, the coach still keeps the original gift as a reminder of a gesture he never expected. How Travis Kelce surprised Porter Ellett with Nike's self-lacing shoesThe friendship began in 2017, when Ellett joined Andy Reid's coaching staff as the senior assistant to the head coach. He handled schedules, meetings and other duties while helping during practice. His role also brought him into regular contact with Chiefs players.Kelce and Ellett quickly connected over their shared interest in sneakers. During one conversation, Kelce mentioned buying Nike's limited-edition self-lacing MAG shoes, inspired by the movie Back to the Future. The pair reportedly cost around $15,000.Ellett then asked Kelce about Nike's next self-lacing model, which was expected to cost around $300. He had a personal reason for wanting them. After losing the use of his right arm, tying his shoes had become difficult."Man, those are perfect for me, because with one hand, it's hard to tie my shoe," Ellett joked during that conversation, as he later recalled to The Kansas City Star.A few months later, Nike released the HyperAdapt 1.0, featuring its Electro Adaptive Reactive Lacing technology. Ellett tried to order a pair online, but they sold out before he could secure them. He mentioned the failed attempt to Kelce and moved on.Then came the surprise. One morning, Ellett found a Nike box waiting at his locker before practice. Inside were the self-lacing shoes he had wanted.Kelce had quietly contacted the Chiefs' equipment managers to get Ellett's shoe size. He then worked through his personal Nike representative to arrange the delivery."I was just shocked more than anything," Ellett told The Kansas City Star in an interview published on February 8, 2024.The gift did not stop at one pair. Kelce eventually arranged two pairs, with the second intended for Andy Reid's brother, Reggie, who had also lost the use of an arm after a motorcycle accident. However, the shoes turned out to be too small for him.Ellett described the gesture as "one of the top things I've ever gotten." He also explained why it meant so much: "He didn't really want to make it anything (of it). That's who he is."Travis Kelce treated Porter Ellett like any other Chiefs teammateThe shoes were not the only reason Ellett remembered Kelce so fondly. During practice, Ellett sometimes threw passes to the tight ends during drills. Some players carefully tossed the ball back to him, but Kelce did not change his approach.He would fire the ball back as usual and tell his teammates, "He's got it." Ellett appreciated that Kelce treated him like everyone else instead of making his disability the focus.Speaking to The Kansas City Star on February 7, 2024, Ellett recalled telling his wife how well Kelce treated people. "With one arm, you realize you can judge a person's character pretty early by how they treat you," he said.Their friendship continued beyond practice. The two sometimes played P-I-G on the basketball hoop in the Chiefs' locker room. Ellett also revealed that Kelce could get frustrated when he lost because of his competitive nature.The story gained wider attention in February 2024 after Ellett's wife, Carlie, shared the shoe story on TikTok. Her video attracted nearly three million views. She wanted to defend Kelce after criticism over his interaction with Ravens kicker Justin Tucker during the AFC Championship Game.Ellett told the newspaper that his wife wanted people to know how Kelce had treated their family. He also revealed that he had kept the original shoes in his closet as a keepsake for his two sons.He once told Kelce, "I gotta tell them the greatest tight end in NFL history gave me a pair of shoes."In Ellett case, the gift became more than a pair of expensive sneakers. articles.body: Tom Brady built his NFL career around winning championships, but one of his most personal commitments had little to do with football. The former New England Patriots quarterback quietly supported organ transplant patients through a charity connected to his late mentor, Tom Martinez. Even after Martinez died in 2012, Brady continued helping the cause through memorabilia auctions and fundraising, keeping a promise that began during one of his coach's toughest battles.The story came to light in a May 10, 2019 report by KTVU. It revealed how Brady continued supporting MatchingDonors.com years after losing the man who helped shape his career. His efforts also gave the Tom Martinez Goal Line Foundation a way to carry that work forward. How Tom Brady stepped in when his mentor needed a kidney transplantBrady's connection to the cause began in 2009. Martinez, who coached Brady at the College of San Mateo, needed a kidney transplant and turned to MatchingDonors.com for help. The nonprofit connects living organ donors with people waiting for transplants.Brady decided to use his public profile to bring attention to the organisation. He spoke about MatchingDonors.com before the Super Bowl and urged people to consider becoming donors. The appeal brought a huge response.Paul Dooley, the organisation's CEO, told KTVU in its May 10, 2019 report that Brady's involvement brought hundreds of potential donors. Seventeen people matched Martinez."Without Tom Martinez there would be no Tom Brady in the NFL," Tom Brady Sr. told KTVU.The coach had played an important role in Brady's development long before he became an NFL star. Martinez worked with him on his quarterback technique, and the two stayed in regular contact. Brady often turned to him whenever he needed help with his game.Their relationship went beyond football. Martinez's health struggle gave Brady a personal reason to support organ donation, and he did not hesitate to use his platform to help.However, the story took a heartbreaking turn in 2012. Martinez died of a heart attack just two weeks before his planned transplant. Despite the loss, Brady did not walk away from the cause. Tom Brady continued raising funds after losing Tom MartinezMartinez's death did not end Brady's involvement with organ donation. According to KTVU, the quarterback continued auctioning memorabilia and raising money in his mentor's memory.Those efforts supported the Tom Martinez Goal Line Foundation, which works to raise awareness about organ donation and support MatchingDonors.com.Dooley also spoke about Brady's continued support during the KTVU report. He explained that Brady helped without waiting for anyone to approach him."He never said no to us. He never said no to the Martinez family. He offered without asking," Dooley told KTVU.He further added, “He does it so quietly. It's amazing. We get checks in the mail and we know it's from him, but we can't tell anyone.”That support carried a personal connection for Brady. His former coach had helped him develop into an NFL quarterback, and he continued to honour that relationship long after Martinez's death.The issue also extended beyond one family. KTVU reported in May 2019 that around 114,000 people were waiting for organ transplants in the United States, while more than 8,000 died each year.Brady's efforts could not solve the organ shortage, but they helped bring attention to a cause that often receives little public coverage. His continued fundraising also gave Martinez's work a lasting purpose.In Brady’s case, the relationship with his former coach did not end when football sessions stopped. Thursday night's prime-time matchup between the Green Bay Packers and the Carolina Panthers had a unplanned pause during the third quarter. With the Packers holding the ball while leading 20-10, the game was interrupted for several minutes as a result of a passing drone, according to the Amazon Prime broadcast.

The unauthorized drone had breached the edge of the stadium, leading the referees to pause the game for safety reasons. Per the broadcast, the teams were told to head back to their respective sidelines while they waited for the drone to leave, with the delay lasting several minutes.

Under Federal Aviation Admisitration (FAA) rules , drones are not allowed within 3 nautical miles of any stadium with more than 30,000 seats, with NFL games specifically mentioned in the guidelines; Green Bay's Lambeau Field has a capacity of 81,441. The rules for drones and model airplanes apply starting one hour before the game until one hour after.

Luckily, the Packers made sure the delay was worth it: On the very next play, quarterback Jordan Love found Josh Jacobs for a touchdown reception to give Green Bay a 27-10 lead. The Packers went on to win 27-19 .

articles.title: Packers Beat Panthers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Bryce Young, Jordan Love, Jacobs, Top Players
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love threw for 288 yards and three touchdowns and the Green Bay defense amassed six sacks en route to a 27-19 home win over the Carolina Panthers on Thursday Night Football.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love threw for 288 yards and three touchdowns and the Green Bay defense amassed six sacks en route to a 27-19 home win over the Carolina Panthers on Thursday Night Football .

The Green Bay Packers were 3.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook . Top Packer fantasy football performers included Love, wideouts Matthew Golden and Christian Watson, running back Josh Jacobs and tight end Tucker Kraft. Panthers running back Chuba Hubbard stood out as well.

Exciting action started on the opening kickoff after Panthers linebacker Jackson Kuwatch stripped Packers kick returner Jackson Owen of the ball, which Carolina LB Nick Hampton recovered on the Green Bay 29-yard line.

Green Bay's defense hung tough, though, and forced a field goal. Ryan Fitzgerald knocked it home from 39 yards for the early 3-0 lead.

The Packers immediately responded with an eight-play, 56-yard touchdown drive. On 3rd-and-8 from the Carolina 12-yard line, Love fired a pass up the middle to Kraft for six.

However, rookie kicker Trey Smack hit the left upright with his PAT. He has now missed three PAT and five field goals (including ones from 26 and 35 yards last Sunday in a 20-17 road loss to the Detroit Lions).

In between the first and second quarters, the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers appeared on the field with the Commissioner's Trophy. Outfielder Sal Frelick even did the Lambeau Leap.

However, Hubbard did a Lambeau leap of his own after he capped a 13-play, 65-yard drive with a one-yard touchdown run. The PAT made it 10-6.

On the Packers' next possession, Watson fumbled after Panthers safety Nick Scott punched the ball out and linebacker Bobby Okereke recovered.

Carolina went three-and-out in response, though, and then Green Bay went downfield for a go-ahead touchdown courtesy of Jacobs on 3rd-and-goal at the Panther one-yard line to cap a nine-play, 90-yard drive.

The big play on the drive was a Watson 53-yard catch despite defensive pass interference from rookie cornerback Will Lee. Watson made a diving catch on a moon ball and fell hard on the ground as Lee landed on top of him while in coverage.

Both were shaken up and went back to the locker room.

Watson suffered a chest injury and was taken to the hospital for precautionary reasons, per sideline reporter Kaylee Hartung during the broadcast. Lee suffered a hamstring injury and did not return.

The Packers got the ball back quickly after linebacker Ty'Ron Hopper deflected Panthers quarterback Bryce Young's pass and caught it himself for the interception to set Green Bay up at the Carolina 43-yard line.

Shortly thereafter, Love hit Golden for a 24-yard touchdown on 3rd-and-13.

The game featured a massive momentum swing early in the third when the Panthers got stuffed on 4th-and-2 at midfield. Packers defensive tackle Chris McClellan got the stop on Hubbard.

Green Bay took advantage of the short field, and Jacobs scored his second touchdown after Love threw him a four-yard pass.

The Packers soon some great news, though, when Watson returned from the hospital after being cleared following tests.

Watson gave more insight into what happened postgame.

As for the game, the Panthers fought back. Ryan Fitzgerald hit a 50-yard field goal late in the third quarter to make it 27-13.

With 5:37 left in regulation and the Panthers facing 4th-and-3 from the Packer 26-yard line, Young hit wide receiver Jalen Coker, who ran in for a touchdown.

Carolina missed a two-point conversion, but a crucial defensive stop led to the Panthers getting the ball back on their own 37-yard line. However, the Green Bay defense showed up again and forced an incomplete pass on 4th-and-5 at midfield.

The Packers ran down the clock nearly all the way, but the Panthers got possession back with 22 seconds remaining and no timeouts. It was a Herculean task to score from there, and the Packers recovered a fumble as the Panthers tried a miracle series of laterals for a touchdown.

Both teams play next on Sunday, Nov. 8. The 5-3 Packers will visit the New England Patriots. The 3-4 Panthers will host the Denver Broncos.

The NFL landscape dramatically changed prior to the start of Week 8 action since some teams already turned into pumpkins before Halloween.

All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson is now a member of the Seattle Seahawks. The Indianapolis Colts also traded defensive lineman DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers. The Chicago Bears raided the AFC South as well by acquiring All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans.

All of that happened before the Carolina Panthers and Green Bay Packers officially took the field for Thursday Night Football .

As always, Bleacher Report NFL analysts Brent Sobleski , Kris Knox , and Moe Moton will follow all of the weekend's action to break down the biggest stories and questions coming out of each contest.

Will the Green Bay Packers Eventually Run The Ball With Any Effectiveness?

The Packers now sit at 5-3 despite fielding the league's worst rushing offense. As the Amazon Prime telecast noted, Green Bay became the first team in NFL history to own a winning record through eight games despite running for fewer than 500 yards.

During Thursday's contest, the Packers barely eclipsed their season-average by running for 66 yards. The team averaged 2.5 yards per carry. Josh Jacobs' return to the lineup has not helped. He carried the ball 32 times for only 75 yards over the last two games.

Yet Green Bay's offense remains competitive, because Jordan Love is playing at a relatively high level despite multiple issues around the quarterback position. Furthermore, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are explosive targets, as long as they hold onto the ball.

Packers' Defense is Only Going to Get Better

Green Bay sacked Carolina Panthers' Bryce Young six times, hit the quarterback nine times and pressured him on 22 dropbacks, according to ESPN Stats & Info (h/t Mike Kaye ).

To understand how dominant the performance was, the Packers accumulated as many sacks as Young completed passes when pressured. Interestingly, each of the quarterback takedowns came from different Green Bay defenders.

The group did this without Micah Parsons in the lineup. Eventually, he's going to return and make the entire unit more potent, even if he's not quite as explosive because opponents will still key on the three-time first-team All-Pro.

Furthermore, Zaire Franklin didn't play Thursday due to a knee injury, but he's not expected to be out long.

Green Bay is flawed, particularly on offense, but the Packers' top 10 defense can carry its share of the responsibility plus more.

Panthers QB Bryce Young Desperately Needs Help

As the calendar flips to November, Young is no longer in the MVP conversation. He was to start the season, but everything has fallen apart around the quarterback.

Carolina's offensive line is a mess. Left guard Damien Lewis didn't play Thursday, and the Panthers certainly felt his absence. Rookie Monroe Freeling remains at right tackle after veteran Taylor Moton suffered a fractured fibula.

Green Bay pressured Young on nearly half of his dropbacks. The Panthers averaged under 3.6 yards per carry. The unit was also incapable of creating explosive plays based on how its currently constructed. As a result, Young has thrown from fewer than 210 yards in back-to-back games

Will Lee III is the latest Panthers cornerback to leave the lineup due to injury.

Based on Carolina's depth chart, the team is now down to its fifth and sixth cornerbacks if someone doesn't return in the short term. Starters Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are already on injured reserve. Throw Akayleb Evans onto that list. Lee is likely out for some time after pulling a hamstring. As a result, Green Bay had little trouble throwing the ball during Thursday's matchup. Watson and Golden combined to grab 15 catches for 192 yards.

The Panthers could be leaning heavily on Chau Smith-Wade and Marco Wilson in the coming weeks unless someone else is signed or brought in via trade.

The calendar officially flips to November and division rivalries kick into overdrive. Seven of Sunday's matchups are between divisional opponents, with the top spots in the AFC North and AFC West up for grabs when the Pittsburgh Steelers host the Cleveland Browns and the Kansas City Chiefs travel to the Mile High City.

NFL teams have already engineered seismic deals in advance of the November 10 trade deadline, but more may be on the horizon.

Following the Green Bay Packers' 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers on Thursday, NFL insider James Palmer reported on Prime about the latest news regarding some contending teams.

Insider: 'All Hell' to Break Loose at Deadline

Kansas City Chiefs: "The Kansas City Chiefs, to my understanding, have been working the phones for weeks here trying to get a wide receiver for Patrick Mahomes. Is that Brian Thomas Jr.? Is that Josh Downs? They've been kind of weighing all their options. [General manager] Brett Veach has done this before, let's see if he can do it again."

Denver Broncos: "They are one of the teams that is monitoring the Jonathan Taylor situation. It's still more likely that he stays there in Indianapolis, but they are keeping an eye there."

Minnesota Vikings: "The Vikings' new general manager, Nolan Teasley, is looking at everything. He's a madman on the phones, I'm told. They're looking at running back and looking at tight end."

In addition, Palmer said the Detroit Lions would "love some cornerback help," and the Pittsburgh Steelers are looking for wide receiver help.

Big names have already changed teams, including left guard Quenton Nelson (to the Seattle Seahawks), defensive tackles Jeffery Simmons (to the Chicago Bears) and DeForest Buckner (to the San Francisco 49ers), Marvin Harrison Jr. (to the Houston Texans) and Joey Porter Jr. (to the Dallas Cowboys). More could be on the way.

Breaking down Palmer's report further, the 5-1 Chiefs need some wide receiver help. Tyquan Thornton leads the wideouts in receiving yards (219), and he has played only four of six games after suffering a dislocated left ankle.

The 5-2 Broncos haven't gotten the run game going, averaging just 3.4 yards per carry. Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (765 total yards, eight touchdowns) would certainly help, although it appears he more likely than not will stay with his current team.

The 6-0 Vikings, who are the last undefeated team remaining, need offensive help. Minnesota has the best scoring defense but sits 23rd in points per game.

The 4-2 Lions have allowed the second-most passing touchdowns (16) and sit 26th in scoring defense.

The 5-2 Steelers' wideout room has been affected by injuries. Roman Wilson (dislocated finger on his left hand) and Michael Pittman Jr. (plantar fasciitis in his left foot) are both on injured reserve.

Overall, expect more movement on a busy trade front as the deadline sits just under two weeks away.

articles.title: Packers WR Christian Watson returns vs. Panthers after leaving game in ambulance coughing up blood with broken rib
articles.summary: Watson left the game before halftime in an ambulance and was back on the field in the third quarter.
articles.body:
A trip to the hospital for coughing up blood did not end Christian Watson's night on the football field.

The Green Bay Packers wide receiver returned to Lambeau Field during Thursday's game against the Carolina Panthers after leaving the first half in an ambulance with a chest injury.

Watson left the hospital around halftime and returned to the game with 4:01 remaining in the third quarter with Green Bay holding a 27-13 lead. He continued to play through the conclusion of the Packers' 27-19 win .

Watson: Football's 'first and foremost to me'

After the game, Watson told the Amazon's Kaylee Hartung that he didn't want to go to the hospital but that team medical staff sent him due to a "couple of signs" indicating that he needed to go. One of those signs was Watson spitting up blood.

"No internal bleeding, no anything that was raising suspicion," Watson said of being cleared to return. "I was spitting a little blood at first, so they just wanted to make sure there was nothing crazy. … I cleared everything and was able to get back out."

Watson added that getting back on the football field was his top priority.

"I'm trying to be out on the football field, that's first and foremost to me," Watson said.

Watson told reporters postgame that he couldn't breath on the field after falling on the ball after a catch. He confirmed that he was "coughing up blood" and that a CT scan revearled a fractured rib.

Doctors cleared him to play with the rib fracture, so he he rushed back to Lambeau Field to finish the game with extra padding around his injury.

"I told them before we even left that I wanted to go back out there, so I was gonna make sure I was gonna be able to get back out there if they let me," Watson said.

The Packers told reporters after halftime that Watson cleared medical testing at a local hospital and was returning to Lambeau Field. At that point he was officially listed as questionable and jogged out of the ambulance upon his return to the stadium.

He then jogged on to the field, much to the delight of the Lambeau Field crowd.

Then, with the Packers holding a 27-13 lead and 4:01 remaining on the third quarter, Watson put on his helmet and returned to the game.

Watson sustained his injury early in the second quarter. He was able to walk off the field and into the ambulance on his own power. The Packers announced that he had sustained a chest injury and was being transported to the hospital for precautionary reasons.

The injury took place on a collision after Watson caught a 53-yard pass in the second quarter.

He remained down on the field for several moments, then walked to the sideline medical tent. After a quick visit in the tent, he walked off the field. He was seen getting into an ambulance moments later.

His night appeared over amid concern about his health. But he was back on the field in the third quarter and finished the game. He caught two more passes after his return, including a late third-down conversion to help ice the Green Bay win.

Watson's in the midst of his best NFL season

Watson is in the midst of a breakout campaign in his fifth NFL season as one of the league's most productive receivers. With eight catches for 113 yards Thursday night, Watson is up to 42 catches for 708 yards and 6 touchdowns this season. His yardage tally is already a career high eight games into the season.

It appears that he'll be able to add to that tally without missing any further time with his injury.

Panthers cornerback Will Lee III collided with Watson on the play and was also injured. He left the field on a cart and did not return due to a hamstring injury.

articles.title: Jordan Love, Matt LaFleur React to Christian Watson's Return from Hospital During Packers' Win
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers players and fans alike were holding their breath in the second quarter of Thursday's game against the Carolina Panthers when Christian Watson was taken out of Lambeau Field in an ambulance.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers players and fans alike were holding their breath in the second quarter of Thursday's game against the Carolina Panthers when Christian Watson was taken out of Lambeau Field in an ambulance .

But by the end of the third quarter, the wide receiver was not only back in the building but on the field.

"Man, that was crazy. It was a lot of people cheering. Stuff was going on," quarterback Jordan Love told reporters . "I didn't know what was happening. Then I see Christian running out, and he's just resurrected. It was great to see him."

Watson finished the 27-19 win with 113 yards on eight receptions. He had 100 yards before exiting in the first half.

"The grit to go back in the game, he had a heck of a night," head coach Matt LaFleur said (4:00 mark). "Can't imagine what he would've had had he not missed so much time."

The injury occurred after Watson caught a deep ball from Love and landed awkwardly. He said that he wanted to return to the game but had to go to the hospital after spitting up blood.

While it was a remarkable comeback for Watson, the injury will surely be something to monitor over the next week as the Packers ensure he's 100 percent before their next game.

articles.title: Touchdown grab stands out amid quiet night for Jalen Coker
articles.summary: Jalen Coker was held to two receptions in Week 8, but he took one of them for a 26-yard touchdown versus the Packers.
articles.body:
Carolina Panthers WR Jalen Coker had two receptions, 36 yards, and a touchdown during the team's Week 8 meeting with the Green Bay Packers . He was targeted five times.

Why It Matters: Coker caught a fourth-down pass late in the game, dodged a would-be tackler and turned a quick crosser into a 26-yard touchdown. It was his only highlight on an otherwise forgettable night. Like basically everyone on Carolina's offense, Coker has seen his production dip the last two weeks as the offensive line struggles to protect Bryce Young long enough for routes to develop downfield. For Coker, Thursday night marked the third time in his last four games that he's finished with fewer than 40 yards. Following a hot start, Coker has slipped back into low-end WR3.

articles.title: Packers’ Christian Watson Suffers Scary Injury Recurrence, Hospitalization Reason Revealed
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson has been through this process before, but it's no less frightening the second time around. The post Packers’...
articles.body:
wide receiver Christian Watson has been one of the most explosive wide receivers in the NFL this season, though he appeared to suffer a familiar injury on Thursday Night Football against the Carolina Panthers that also knocked him out of commission during a contest back in December of 2025.

David J. Chao, a former lead team doctor in the league for upwards of two decades, shared video replay of Watson's injury in the second quarter of the game at Lambeau Field on October 29.

"Christian Watson: Sent to the hospital for fear of a sternoclavicular [SC] joint sprain," Chao posted to X . "Similar to last year."

Watson was injured on a 53-yard completion from quarterback Jordan Love with just over nine minutes remaining in the second quarter. It was Watson's sixth catch of the night and boosted his receiving total to 100 yards .

However, his exit from the contest and subsequent trip to the hospital ended his evening after that play.

Christian Watson Suffered Similar Injury Against Denver in Week 15 of Last Season, Returned in Following Game

Watson suffered a similar injury against the Denver Broncos in Week 15 of last season, which was the same game in which pass-rusher Micah Parsons suffered his torn ACL.

Watson also left that game early and boarded an ambulance to the hospital, as team doctors were concerned the wideout may have suffered a SC joint dislocation or clavicle fracture. The area is highly sensitive, as nerves, arteries, the esophagus and the trachea are all located in the vicinity of the SC joint.

Fortunately for Watson, he was able to return the following week against the Chicago Bears and play in Week 17 against the Baltimore Ravens . He sat out Week 18 due to a coach's decision, then suited up for the Packers wildcard playoff game at Soldier Field in Chicago.

UPDATE: Watson returned from the hospital and to the sideline at Lambeau Field as of the middle of the third quarter, jogging out under his own power. He appeared poised to return to the action, which means doctors likely cleared him of the dangerous potential symptoms described below.

Christian Watson's Trip to Hospital About Making Sure Blood Vessels in Chest Weren't Impacted by Hit

Chao went on to explain the unlikely, but dire, risk that a severe SC joint can have — mainly because of how it can impact major blood vessels in the chest.

"Watson went down on his left shoulder, sent to the hospital. Why? If it's a standard shoulder injury, you don't go to the hospital," Chao said in a follow-up video . "Part of the reason is if you have an SC joint … there is some risk if you have it dislocated that it presses on the great vessels in your chest. This is one to be careful of. Probably isn't, but you always wanna be safe than sorry."

If Watson did not suffer an SC sprain, he will likely be able to return against the New England Patriots for the Packers' Week 9 contest on November 8 in Foxborough.

Watson has tallied 40 catches for 695 receiving yards and six TDs this season. If he can avoid a serious injury, the wideout is on pace for by far the best campaign of his five-year NFL career.

articles.title: Cowboys’ CeeDee Lamb Doubles Down on Bold Warning
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys star receiver CeeDee Lamb explained why he warned NFL defenses during last week's win over the Eagles.. The post Cowboys’ CeeDee Lamb Doubles...
articles.body:
During the heat of battle on Monday night, in a primetime game against the rival Eagles, Dallas Cowboys star receiver CeeDee Lamb was feeling his oats. He had caught a spectacular touchdown and added another, making five catches for 74 yards overall. He taunted the crowd and, after the game during an interview with Scott Van Pelt of ESPN, noted how much he hated the Eagles and their backers. In the midst of the game, Lamb caught attention for a pretty bold declaration made to NFL defenses on his talents.

Roaming the sidelines as NFL cameras rolled, Lamb warned any defenders in earshot, "You can't move. You can't touch—like, nobody in this world, on this planet that live on the planet that we live on, they cannot stick in front of me. I said it to the world, nobody did it yet. And now I say it again. Can't guard me."

Again, that was in the heat of battle on Monday. In the calm of a midweek press conference out at The Star, Cowboys reporters asked Lamb about that clip, which made the rounds on social media.

Lamb explained why, exactly, no one on the planet can guard him: "I think my ability to line up anywhere in the offense and run any route on the route tree. I feel like I can beat anybody in front of me. I'm gonna stand on that."

Lamb also noted that when the Cowboys offense is rolling–which has been the case only sporadically this season it is generally difficult to guard.

He noted: "It's almost like it is inevitable because regardless what coverage you put on it, there is nothing blanketing it. You have an option, you have an answer for every coverage. I feel like in that realm, as an offensive player, you like it because it is like the mercy is in your court."

Cowboys Winless vs. Arizona in WR's Career

If there is a time for some humility from Lamb, though, it will be this week entering Sunday's Week 8 game against the Cardinals . In four tries during his NFL career, Lamb has gone 0-4 against Arizona.

He noted that the Cowboys have taken them too lightly in the past, and that the Cardinals have been amped up for the matchup from the get go. "We've been very relaxed and they've punched us in the mouth every single time," Lamb said.

articles.title: UConn Women's Basketball: When Are Huskies Alums Playing in WNBA Game 7?
articles.summary: The Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream will meet on Saturday night.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream defeated the Golden State Valkyries (80-69) in Game 6 of the WNBA Finals on Thursday afternoon, forcing a Game 7 that is set for Saturday night at 8 p.m. ET in Golden State.

This will be the first-ever Game 7 in WNBA Finals history, as the league just adopted a best-of-seven championship series in 2025.

Several former UConn Huskies women's basketball alums will be representing Golden State in its quest to win the first title in franchise history:

Kaitlyn Chen, Tiffany Hayes, Kiah Stokes and Gabby Williams all play for Golden State. This is just the second year that the franchise has existed.

Chen played three years of college basketball at Princeton before transferring to UConn for her senior year in 2024-25. With the Huskies, she played and started 40 games, averaging 6.9 ppg and 3.4 assists. She helped the Huskies win the national title alongside Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd and was drafted No. 30 overall in the 2025 WNBA Draft.

She was the Ivy League Player of the Year in 2022-23 at Princeton. She played just five minutes in the Game 6 loss. She averaged 7.2 ppg in the regular season.

Williams, the most decorated former Huskies star on the Valkyries, is also an incredibly accomplished WNBA player. She had 26 points, three rebounds and three steals on Thursday.

A four-year standout for the Huskies, Williams crossed over with legendary forward Breanna Stewart for two of UConn's four straight national titles (2015 and 2016). She started 85 games in Storrs, getting named Defensive Player of the Year in 2017. She was also a two-time Associated Press All-American and a two-time All-AAC selection. She averaged 10.6 ppg for her career and was the No. 4 overall pick in the 2018 WNBA Draft (Chicago Sky).

She's also represented France on the international stage, leading the French to the Olympic silver medal in 2024 and a second-place finish at this year's FIBA World Cup.

Hayes scored 15 points in 28 minutes on Thursday. She won two national titles at UConn in 2008-09 and 2009-10. She played in 154 games with the Huskies, averaging 11.7 ppg for her career. An All-American in her senior year, she was also a three-time All-Big East selection who was drafted No. 14 overall in the 2012 WNBA Draft. Ironically, she was taken by the Dream and spent 10 years there before also playing with Las Vegas, Connecticut and Golden State.

Another starter for Golden State, she had zero points in 20 minutes on Thursday. She averaged 3.6 ppg and 5.8 rebounds a game this season.

A three-time national champion at UConn, she also had crossover with Stewart and Williams. She averaged 4.5 ppg for her career and was the 2014-15 AAC Defensive Player of the Year. She was taken No. 11 overall in 2015 by the New York Liberty.

articles.title: Jerry Jones once explained why Donald Trump was ‘problematic’ for the NFL
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones once admitted that Donald Trump’s involvement in the NFL’s national anthem debate was damaging to the league, describing the...
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones once admitted that Donald Trump's involvement in the NFL's national anthem debate was damaging to the league, describing the president's interest as "problematic".

Jones made the comments in 2018, when the NFL was attempting to resolve the controversy surrounding players kneeling during the national anthem to protest racial injustice.

The debate had become a major talking point after Trump publicly criticised players who protested and urged the league to punish those who refused to stand.

Jerry Jones admitted Donald Trump's comments were problematic for the NFL

Speaking at the Cowboys' training camp in California, Jones acknowledged that Trump's comments were creating difficulties for NFL owners.

"His interest in what we're doing is problematic from my chair, and I would say in general the owners' chair," Jones said.

He also admitted that owners wanted the controversy to end, adding: "It's unprecedented if you really think about it. Yes I would like — everybody would like — for it to go away."

Jones was not the only NFL owner to express concerns. Cincinnati Bengals owner Mike Brown also suggested that Trump's comments had worked against the league, claiming the debate had made people view the NFL unfavourably.

However, Jones maintained that the Cowboys would expect their players to stand during the national anthem, making the team's position clear despite the wider disagreement.

"It did not impact our position," he said. "Our position is very clear in that you should stand."

The comments came amid wider tensions between the NFL and its players' association over the league's proposed anthem policy. The NFLPA had argued that the policy infringed on players' rights, while discussions between the two sides continued.

The controversy also raised concerns among sponsors and team owners, particularly as reports suggested NFL television ratings had declined during the previous season.

Jones had owned the Cowboys since 1989, and the franchise's commercial success meant that any damage to the league's popularity was a significant concern.

His comments offered a glimpse into the difficult position NFL owners faced as Trump's criticism brought the national anthem debate back into the spotlight.
